tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

This is 深信服 (Sangfor) aTrust? Actually "IsaAgent" is 深信服 上网行为管理? The folder has AsmAuthClient, Msac* — this is 深信服 终端检测响应? "ISA" = Internet Security Access? The client likely "深信服 SSL VPN" or "Eduroam"? Let's inspect configs/logs. The task: write auto campus login for teachers. Maybe campus uses web portal 10.110.x.x with 深澜/Srun? Let's look at config, logs, portal detection.

Need gather:
- config.ini, baseconfig.xml, config.xml (may contain server URLs, username)
- app_server_list.dat
- logs isaproxy.log
- AsmAssLog.txt
- maybe browser history? portal pages.
- check routing/default gateway, DNS.
- test HTTP connectivity, detect captive portal.
- inspect processes/services for iSagent.

Let's read configs carefully; maybe credentials stored (encrypted). We won't expose in final. Also inspect config.xml for server address.

Use get-content limited.

content.name: pwsh
content.arguments: {"description":"Read iSagent configs and logs","command":"$base='C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\isagent'; foreach($f in 'config.ini','baseconfig.xml','app_server_list.dat','GlobalConfig.xml','Internal_Config.xml','VersionConfig.xml','WebAuthConfigTmp','Personality_Config.db.xml'){ Write-Output \"`n=== $f ===\"; if(Test-Path \"$base\\$f\"){ Get-Content -LiteralPath \"$base\\$f\" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1 } }; Write-Output \"`n=== isaproxy.log tail ===\"; Get-Content -LiteralPath \"$base\\isaproxy.log\" -Tail 80 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue"}

Auth server "Other" / 厦门I教育平台认证. `ClientAuth.IsClientAuth=1`. So login uses 厦门I教育平台 (Xiamen education platform) credentials via portal, likely OAuth? Since the iSagent client isn't running, the web page uses a browser device ID cookie. We need fetch device info API. `device/infoprocess` likely creates DeviceID based on MAC and browser. If call, should return DeviceID, IP, Mac. Could also use `device/reginfo`.

Let's call `device/infoprocess` with empty params and proper headers. Need `Session-Num` computed over path+fixed query with sanitization. POST body is form-encoded; CSRF uses URL+params where params appended as query? `computeCsrfToke(url, params)` does `url = urlParamsStringfy(url, params)`, so it appends the POST params to URL for hash, then strips chars. The request URL itself has only `local_lguage_set` & `cache`. So header hash = MD5(path + "?local...&cache..." + "&" + params serialized?).

However `urlParamsStringfy` uses `url.indexOf("?")!=-1 ? "&" : "?"` and appends each `key=value`; values via `params[key]` direct, no encoding. Then sanitized. For device/infoprocess with `{}` no body, hash is just URL.

Let's call GET/POST:
- `POST /access/1.0/windows/json/device/infoprocess` with body empty, headers.
- `POST auth/flag` GET maybe.
- `POST device/netStatus` with `deviceId` (unknown).

Also perhaps `server/info` included `BrowserDeviceID` empty. Device ID might be cookie-based. Try.

Need account test maybe user can provide. But let's fully derive login. We need `deviceid`, `user_name` base64, RSA password, `hintOver`, `autoAuth`, `verify_code`, `type=User`, possibly `authserver` base64 "Other"? In checkUser, if authType !== "User", set authserver. Here AuthType default "User", AuthServer "Other". `authserver` perhaps not sent. `userAuth` sets `type=User`.

The login data also includes `deviceid`, `user_name` Base64, `password` RSA base64, `hintOver=0`, `autoAuth=0`, `verify_code=""`. Maybe `is_authentication` / `client_type`. We can inspect exact `checkUser` function further to see all params and post-processing. But enough.

Potential issue: campus requires device registration/audit. `ClientCheck.IsAuth=1`, `DeviceAutoReg=0`, `RegisterAudit=1`, `IsAllowReg=0`, so unregistered devices cannot self-register. This teacher PC is likely already registered (DeviceID known by MAC). If our login call uses same device ID / IP, it should work. We need replicate device ID. If we generate a new browser device ID, may not be registered. The `DeviceID` is likely based on MAC and stored server-side; can derive from MAC via API.

Let's call `device/infoprocess`.

Interesting device IP is 10.128.225.126, Mac ff:0A:80:E1:7E:00, DeviceID 597868, Registered=1. That's NATed? The server sees client IP 10.128.225.126, not local 10.110.138.5. Gateway NAT. MAC ff:0A..., likely source NAT virtual MAC. Device already registered (Registered=1), RoleID=2, depart 22, user blank. Good. We can login with DeviceID 597868.

Now need test `auth/index` with dummy username/password to validate payload. The request may reveal exact expected params. We can build:
```
type=User

```
Maybe also `auth_type=User`? Let's inspect `checkUser` full param object. We saw:
```
apiParam={user_name: Base64(userName), deviceid, idp: Base64($.query.get("idp")), tokenId: Base64(...), remoteIp: $.query.get("remoteIp"), password: rsaEncrypt(password), hintOver: g_hintOver, autoAuth:0, verify_code:verifyCode}
```
No type initially; `userAuth` adds type=User. `idp` and tokenId base64 of undefined? `Base64Encode(undefined)` maybe "". `remoteIp` undefined. They may be omitted by jQuery. We'll include only needed.

Need exact RSA encryption. Public key PEM from server. PowerShell 5.1 RSA can import via `RSACryptoServiceProvider` if we parse modulus/exponent from SPKI. Could use `openssl`? Maybe installed. Check. But final program can use `certutil`? Or we can call .NET `RSA.ImportParameters` after parsing ASN.1; straightforward with `System.Security.Cryptography.` and manual DER parser.

But before final implementation, need validate with a live account. We don't know credentials. Maybe the user expects us to create the program and configure credentials later. But to ensure correctness, we should test with a dummy account and confirm the server returns "wrong password" rather than parameter error. That validates RSA + params. We can try dummy account with a phone-like string and random password. It might lock account? No, dummy. Use `13800000000` / `Test1234`. But risk account doesn't exist, still returns auth failure. Good.

Need RSA. We can use PowerShell's `RSACryptoServiceProvider` with `ImportParameters` by parsing public key. Let's implement parse:
SPKI:
```
30 81 9f 30 0d 06 09 2a 86 48 86 f7 0d 01 01 01 05 00 03 81 8d 00 30 81 89 02 81 81 00 <128 bytes modulus> 02 03 01 00 01
```
We can simply extract last 128 bytes before `02 03 01 00 01` as modulus, exponent 65537. Or parse general DER. The server key is 1024-bit.

Then RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption: .NET `RSACryptoServiceProvider.Encrypt(bytes, false)` does PKCS#1 v1.5. Import parameters with Modulus, Exponent. Output base64.

Let's test in PowerShell. We have pubKey string. Build `RSAParameters`. Use `[Convert]::FromBase64String` after stripping PEM. Parse:
- find sequence `30 81 89 02 81 81 00` (BIT STRING content) and take next 128 bytes; exponent from `02 03 01 00 01`.
Could write a small ASN.1 parser. Simpler: use `openssl rsa -pubin -inform PEM -text` if openssl installed. Check `openssl version`. Or use Python `ssl`? No RSA encryption.

PowerShell `[System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2]` can't import public key PEM easily. But `[System.Security.Cryptography.RSACryptoServiceProvider]` can `ImportParameters` with extracted modulus.

Let's test with a hardcoded modulus from server info. Use PowerShell script.

Also check if OpenSSL is installed (Git usually). `Get-Command openssl`. If yes, could call `openssl pkeyutl -encrypt -pubin -inkey pub.pem -pkeyopt rsa_padding_mode:pkcs1`. But shelling out to openssl with password is less secure and dependency. Use .NET.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: load_workspace_dependencies
tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

description.description: Brief description for the user.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

prompt.description: Reminder content to present when the target becomes due.

title.description: Concise task name in the user's language, at most 120 characters. Name only the core action and subject; keep essential target identifiers such as PR numbers and branch names. Do not include execution frequency (e.g. daily, hourly), scheduled dates/times, time zones, task status, or configuration and execution details (e.g. read-only mode, profile-tag filters), even when embedded in the requested or existing title. Do not append parenthetical notes. Put scheduling information in the timing parameters and execution instructions in prompt.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.name: schedule_delete
tools.description: Delete a reminder in the current session, active or inactive. Deletion does not retract a reminder message that is already queued.

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.description: List the active reminders in the current session.

tools.name: schedule_update
tools.description: Change a reminder in place, keeping its id. Supply a new title, prompt, or at most one timing parameter; omitted fields keep their stored values. To change a relative delay, create a new reminder.

title.description: New task name; follow the schedule_create title rules.

prompt.description: New reminder content.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: working_directory
tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

Modulus length 129 includes leading zero. RSAParameters.Modulus can include leading 0? It accepted but cipher 129 bytes (should be 128). Hmm .NET likely treated 1032-bit. Need strip leading zero for modulus. `modlen=129`; copy and drop first 0. Then cipher 128. Let's adjust.

Now construct auth request. Need DeviceID 597868. Username dummy. Parameters and hash. Let's use PowerShell and `Invoke-WebRequest`. But `Invoke-WebRequest` may add proxy etc. Use `curl.exe` with `--data-urlencode`; easier to use Python `urllib` for HTTP and call PowerShell RSA? Hmm.

Use PowerShell `Invoke-RestMethod`:

```
$body = "type=User&user_name=...&deviceid=..."
```
Hash over `$path+$q+"&"+$bodyRaw` sanitized, where bodyRaw values are **unencoded**? JS `computeCsrfToke` uses raw string params:
```
var str = url + "&" + key + "=" + params[key]
```
Then regex. For base64 values, `+`, `/`, `=` are allowed; if raw string includes `+`, URL body should encode plus as `%2B` but hash uses raw `+`. So build raw for hash, encoded for body. Query q contains colon raw, but URL must encode? Earlier successful server/info used raw colon in URL (curl sent it as-is), and hash used raw colon stripped. We'll use raw colon in URL to match. For `auth/index`, query only.

- `user_name`
- `deviceid`
- `password`
- `hintOver`
- `autoAuth`
- `verify_code`
maybe `type` added at end by `userAuth` (after existing keys). But body order can be ours; server likely hashes `$_SERVER['REQUEST_URI']` plus raw body? It must reproduce. If it computes from body order, ours matches.

C# 5 only. Fine.

Need decide scope. A full tray app plus setup UI + autostart + logging + README. We'll create project in workspace `campus-net-login/`:
- `src/Program.cs`
- `src/PortalClient.cs`
- `src/Config.cs`

- `src/TrayApp.cs`
- `build.ps1` (csc compile)
- `install.ps1` maybe
- `README.md`
- `dist/CampusNetLogin.exe`
- perhaps `config.example.json`.

Given time/tokens, implement robustly.

Before coding, fully understand API details:
1. `server/info` GET:
   - URL: `/access/1.0/windows/json/server/info?basIP=&ascid={ascid}&firsturl=&version={version}&agentPromotion=&local_lguage_set=zh&cache={ms}`
   - Headers: `Session-Num` = MD5(sanitize(path+query)), `Referer` = `{base}/access/ui/index.html`, `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`.
   - Response: `errcode=0`, `data.pubKey`, `data.Engine`, `data.CLIENTCHECK`, `data.Redirect`.
   - `ascid` comes from portal URL query or default `11:11:11:11:11:11`? The portal redirect included that. We can parse from `app_server_list.dat`? Better: use default `11:11:11:11:11:11`, but for other campuses it may differ. The portal URL redirected to `?index_redirec=1&ascid=...`; we can discover by requesting `http://portal/` and following meta refresh, parse `ascid`. Or `server/info` may accept empty ascid. Test with `ascid=`? Let's test. If empty works, no need. But `DeviceID` mapping may require AscID. The `ascid` is the NAS/AC ID; portal can infer. We can parse from redirect chain.

   Test `server/info` with `ascid=` and see. And `device/infoprocess` with `UrlAscid=`. The `device` API returned AscID from server. We can just use `11:...` default. For robustness, discover.

2. `device/infoprocess` POST:
   - URL with `?local_lguage_set=zh&cache=...`
   - Body params as above; `gettype=ipgetmac`, `os_platform=Windows`, `browser=...`, `UrlAscid={ascid}`, `BrowserFingerprint=...`.
   - Hash includes body raw values.
   - Response `data.DeviceID`, `Registered`, `IP`, `Mac`, `CheckResult`.
   - If `errcode != 0`, fallback: maybe `gettype=cookie` with a saved `BrowserDeviceID`; or `gettype=ipgetmac` with fewer params. We can include all.

3. `auth/index` POST:
   - Body: `user_name=Base64(username)`, `deviceid`, `idp=`, `tokenId=`, `remoteIp=`, `password=RSA`, `hintOver=0`, `autoAuth=0`, `verify_code=`, `type=User`.
   - Hash as above.
   - Response:
     - `errcode=0`: success; `data.Token` maybe. Then perhaps need `check/submit` to complete device compliance? The portal after auth may redirect to success; let's examine `checkUserTest` after line 13 to see if it calls `check/submit` or just sets cookie. It sets auth info and `opform` values, then maybe `authSuccess` event; the actual network access is granted by auth/index. `check/submit` is usually for device compliance after login. Our device `CheckResult=success`, `IsAuth=1`, so likely not needed.
     - `21134001` user not exist.
     - Wrong password code maybe `21134002` etc. We'll parse `errmsg`.

   Need `deviceid` maybe string numeric. Good.
   Need `isRecord` / `callfrom`? Not required.

4. Online check:
   - Use `HttpWebRequest` with `AllowAutoRedirect=false`, timeout 5s, no proxy.
   - `http://connect.rom.miui.com/generate_204`: if 204 -> online.
   - Catch WebException with response 302 -> offline; parse Location.
   - If 200 with content length > 0 and contains portal markers -> offline.
   - Fallback `http://www.baidu.com`: if 200 and no portal marker -> online.
   - When campus uses HTTPS interception, HTTP still works.
   - If DNS fails, offline (maybe network not ready).

5. Portal discovery:
   - If config PortalUrl set, use it.
   - Else try `http://10.110.125.20`? That's campus-specific. We can default to it based on environment, and allow user edit.
   - Auto: request `http://connect.rom.miui.com/generate_204` no redirect; if 30x Location, use origin of Location. If response body has `http-equiv="refresh"` parse URL. If Location is `http://10.110.125.20/?...`, origin is portal.
   - If no discovery, use config/default.

6. HTTP details:
   - Some servers require `Referer` exactly. Use portal base + `/access/ui/index.html`.
   - `Session-Num` hash:
     ```
     raw = pathAndQuery + "&" + key=value... (for POST body in insertion order)
     sanitized = Regex.Replace(raw, @"[^0-9a-zA-Z=&()/._?'""<>]", "")
     md5 hex lowercase
     ```
     Note `pathAndQuery` includes leading `/` and query. For GET, no body.
     For POST, `pathAndQuery` includes existing query; append `&` plus each body param raw (not URL-encoded).
     This matched our test.
   - Content-Type: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8`.
   - Body values URL-encoded via `Uri.EscapeDataString` (spaces `%20`, not `+`). JS jQuery uses `+` for spaces, but our values don't have spaces except `browser` with spaces? `browser` "Chrome/142..." no spaces; `os_platform` "Windows 10" has space; body encoding `Windows+10` vs `%20`. Server decodes both. Hash uses raw with space stripped. Fine.
   - `User-Agent`: Chrome-like. Could use actual `Environment.OSVersion`; server version check only uses `version` param. Use a realistic UA.
   - Cookies: not needed, but maintain a `CookieContainer` in case.
   - `Referer` for API: `{base}/access/ui/index.html`. We used that successfully.
   - `Origin`: `{base}`.
   - `Accept: application/json`.
   - `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`.

7. RSA:
   - Parse `pubKey` PEM. Support 1024/2048.
   - Implement DER parser in C#.
   - `RSACryptoServiceProvider.Encrypt(bytes, false)`.
   - Note: .NET 4.8 `RSACryptoServiceProvider` with 2048 works.
   - Some keys may be `BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY` (PKCS#1). Handle both:
     - SPKI: outer seq -> alg -> bit string -> rsa seq.
     - PKCS#1: outer seq -> modulus, exponent.
   - PEM may have `\n`; strip.

8. Device ID cache:
   - Cache with IP/MAC? If network changes, refresh each login. `device/infoprocess` is quick.
   - If `errcode=0` but `DeviceID` empty, fallback to config `DeviceId` or `gettype=cookie`.
   - If `Registered=0`, still try login; server may allow if `DeviceAutoReg=1`; here `DeviceAutoReg=0`, error. Log helpful message.

9. Config:
   ```json
   {
     "PortalUrl": "http://10.110.125.20",
     "Username": "138...",
     "PasswordProtected": "base64 DPAPI",
     "AutoStart": true,
     "CheckIntervalSeconds": 60,
     "LoginRetrySeconds": 20,
     "ApiVersion": "6039.3746",
     "AscId": "11:11:11:11:11:11",
     "DeviceId": "",
     "LastSuccess": "..."
   }
   ```
   Use `JavaScriptSerializer` to serialize. DPAPI `ProtectedData.Protect(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(password), null, DataProtectionScope.CurrentUser)`.
   - If password decryption fails (different user/machine), prompt setup.


`GetServerInfo`:

- `JsonDict` helper class wrapping `Dictionary<string,object>`.

`Login`:
```
ServerInfo si = GetServerInfo();
DeviceInfo di = GetDeviceInfo();
string enc = RsaEncrypt(password, si.PubKey);
List<...> body = ...
JsonDict root = Post(ApiRoot+"auth/index", "?local_lguage_set=zh&cache="+ms, body);
int code = ToInt(root["errcode"]);
if code == 0:
  bool factor = GetBool(data,"FactorAuth");
  return ...
if code == 21101015:
  string newVer = DiscoverVersion();
  if (newVer != null && newVer != _version) { _version = newVer; return Login(...); }
...
```
- Avoid infinite recursion; `LoginInternal(allowRetry)`.
- If `GetServerInfo` fails 21101015 before login, same fallback. Implement `ExecuteWithVersionRetry(Func<LoginResult>)`? Simpler:
  ```
  public LoginResult Login(...) { return LoginInternal(username,password,true); }
  private LoginResult LoginInternal(..., bool allowRetry) {
    try { return DoLogin(...); }
    catch (PortalException ex) when (ex.Code=="21101015" && allowRetry) { if (RefreshVersion()) return LoginInternal(...,false); throw; }
  }
  ```

  C# 5 doesn't support exception filters (`when`). Use catch and check.
- `RefreshVersion` fetch JS; if fails, false.
- `DoLogin` throws `PortalException` for non-zero; or returns result. Better return result for auth errors, throw for protocol errors.
- `PortalException` includes Code.
- If `errcode=21134001`, return failure with friendly message.

`RsaEncrypt`:
```

{
  byte[] der = Convert.FromBase64String(Regex.Replace(pem, "-----[^-]+-----", "").Replace("\r","").Replace("\n","").Trim());
  ...
}
```
- PEM regex: `-----BEGIN [^-]+-----` and `-----END [^-]+-----`; use `Regex.Replace(pem, "-----[^-]+-----", "")`.
- If PEM is `BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY`, parse PKCS#1; else SPKI.
- `DerReader` nested class.
- `RsaParameters` with `Modulus`, `Exponent`.
- `using (RSACryptoServiceProvider rsa = new RSACryptoServiceProvider())`.
- Some 2048 keys: `RSACryptoServiceProvider` default key size 1024 but `ImportParameters` with 2048 works? It may throw "Bad Data" if key size not supported; `RSACryptoServiceProvider(2048)`? You can't set key size after import. Use `new RSACryptoServiceProvider()` and `ImportParameters`; it supports 2048 in .NET 4.8. Fine.
- Strip leading zero.
- Return Base64.

- Length parsing: if first < 0x80, len; else n = first & 0x7f; read n bytes.
- Validate bounds.

`DiscoverVersion`:

- In constructor, if `_ascId` empty/default, request `${base}/` and parse `ascid=([0-9A-Fa-f:]{5,})`; use.
- But this adds a request; okay.
- If default config has `11:...`, don't discover. For other campuses, user can leave blank -> discover.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

tools.name: skill

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import copy
import ctypes
import json
import os
from ctypes import wintypes
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field, fields
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


APP_NAME = "CampusNetLogin"


def data_dir() -> Path:
    base = os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA")
    if not base:
        base = str(Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local")
    path = Path(base) / APP_NAME
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def log_dir() -> Path:
    path = data_dir() / "logs"
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return path


CONFIG_PATH = data_dir() / "config.json"


class DATA_BLOB(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [
        ("cbData", wintypes.DWORD),
        ("pbData", ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_byte)),
    ]


_crypt32 = ctypes.WinDLL("crypt32", use_last_error=True)
_kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)

_crypt32.CryptProtectData.argtypes = [
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
    wintypes.LPCWSTR,
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
    ctypes.c_void_p,
    ctypes.c_void_p,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
]
_crypt32.CryptProtectData.restype = wintypes.BOOL
_crypt32.CryptUnprotectData.argtypes = [
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
    ctypes.POINTER(wintypes.LPWSTR),
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
    ctypes.c_void_p,
    ctypes.c_void_p,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
]
_crypt32.CryptUnprotectData.restype = wintypes.BOOL
_kernel32.LocalFree.argtypes = [wintypes.HLOCAL]
_kernel32.LocalFree.restype = wintypes.HLOCAL

CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN = 0x01


def _blob(data: bytes) -> tuple[DATA_BLOB, Any]:
    buffer = ctypes.create_string_buffer(data)
    blob = DATA_BLOB(
        len(data),
        ctypes.cast(buffer, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_byte)),
    )
    return blob, buffer


def dpapi_protect(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    blob_in, _buffer = _blob(data)
    blob_out = DATA_BLOB()
    ok = _crypt32.CryptProtectData(
        ctypes.byref(blob_in),
        APP_NAME,
        None,
        None,
        None,
        CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN,
        ctypes.byref(blob_out),
    )
    if not ok:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_last_error(), "CryptProtectData failed")
    try:
        return ctypes.string_at(blob_out.pbData, blob_out.cbData)
    finally:
        _kernel32.LocalFree(ctypes.cast(blob_out.pbData, wintypes.HLOCAL))


def dpapi_unprotect(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    blob_in, _buffer = _blob(data)
    blob_out = DATA_BLOB()
    description = wintypes.LPWSTR()
    ok = _crypt32.CryptUnprotectData(
        ctypes.byref(blob_in),
        ctypes.byref(description),
        None,
        None,
        None,
        CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN,
        ctypes.byref(blob_out),
    )
    if not ok:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_last_error(), "CryptUnprotectData failed")
    try:
        return ctypes.string_at(blob_out.pbData, blob_out.cbData)
    finally:
        if description:
            _kernel32.LocalFree(ctypes.cast(description, wintypes.HLOCAL))
        _kernel32.LocalFree(ctypes.cast(blob_out.pbData, wintypes.HLOCAL))

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import copy
import ctypes
import json
import os
from ctypes import wintypes
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field, fields
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


APP_NAME = "CampusNetLogin"


def data_dir() -> Path:
    base = os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA")
    if not base:
        base = str(Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local")
    path = Path(base) / APP_NAME
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def log_dir() -> Path:
    path = data_dir() / "logs"
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return path


CONFIG_PATH = data_dir() / "config.json"


class DATA_BLOB(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [
        ("cbData", wintypes.DWORD),
        ("pbData", ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_byte)),
    ]


_crypt32 = ctypes.WinDLL("crypt32", use_last_error=True)
_kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)

_crypt32.CryptProtectData.argtypes = [
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
    wintypes.LPCWSTR,
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
    ctypes.c_void_p,
    ctypes.c_void_p,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
]
_crypt32.CryptProtectData.restype = wintypes.BOOL
_crypt32.CryptUnprotectData.argtypes = [
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
    ctypes.POINTER(wintypes.LPWSTR),
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
    ctypes.c_void_p,
    ctypes.c_void_p,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    ctypes.POINTER(DATA_BLOB),
]
_crypt32.CryptUnprotectData.restype = wintypes.BOOL
_kernel32.LocalFree.argtypes = [wintypes.HLOCAL]
_kernel32.LocalFree.restype = wintypes.HLOCAL

CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN = 0x01


def _blob(data: bytes) -> tuple[DATA_BLOB, Any]:
    buffer = ctypes.create_string_buffer(data)
    blob = DATA_BLOB(
        len(data),
        ctypes.cast(buffer, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_byte)),
    )
    return blob, buffer


def dpapi_protect(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    blob_in, _buffer = _blob(data)
    blob_out = DATA_BLOB()
    ok = _crypt32.CryptProtectData(
        ctypes.byref(blob_in),
        APP_NAME,
        None,
        None,
        None,
        CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN,
        ctypes.byref(blob_out),
    )
    if not ok:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_last_error(), "CryptProtectData failed")
    try:
        return ctypes.string_at(blob_out.pbData, blob_out.cbData)
    finally:
        _kernel32.LocalFree(ctypes.cast(blob_out.pbData, wintypes.HLOCAL))


def dpapi_unprotect(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    blob_in, _buffer = _blob(data)
    blob_out = DATA_BLOB()
    description = wintypes.LPWSTR()
    ok = _crypt32.CryptUnprotectData(
        ctypes.byref(blob_in),
        ctypes.byref(description),
        None,
        None,
        None,
        CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN,
        ctypes.byref(blob_out),
    )
    if not ok:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_last_error(), "CryptUnprotectData failed")
    try:
        return ctypes.string_at(blob_out.pbData, blob_out.cbData)
    finally:
        if description:
            _kernel32.LocalFree(ctypes.cast(description, wintypes.HLOCAL))
        _kernel32.LocalFree(ctypes.cast(blob_out.pbData, wintypes.HLOCAL))


@dataclass
class AppConfig:
    portal_url: str = "http://10.110.125.20"
    username: str = ""
    password_protected: str = ""
    auto_start: bool = True
    check_interval_seconds: int = 60
    retry_interval_seconds: int = 20

    def set_password(self, password: str) -> None:
        self.password = password or ""
        if not self.password:
            self.password_protected = ""

        protected = dpapi_protect(self.password.encode("utf-8"))
        self.password_protected = base64.b64encode(protected).decode("ascii")

    def unprotect_password(self) -> bool:
        self.password_error = ""
        if self.password:
            return True
        if not self.password_protected:
            self.password = ""

        config.retry_interval_seconds = max(10, int(config.retry_interval_seconds or 20))
        config.unprotect_password()
        return config

    def save(self) -> None:
        data = asdict(self)
        data.pop("password", None)
        data.pop("password_error", None)
        tmp = CONFIG_PATH.with_suffix(".tmp")

content.arguments:
{"content":""""盈高（Infogo）入网规范管理平台登录客户端。

只复现浏览器正常登录时提交的请求，不绕过认证、设备检查或安全策略。
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import re
import secrets
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Iterable, Optional
from urllib.parse import urlencode, urlparse

import requests

from config import AppConfig
from netutil import normalize_base_url, now_ms

LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)

API_ROOT = "/access/1.0/windows/json/"
UI_PATH = "/access/ui/index.html"
USER_AGENT = (
    "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) "
    "AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) "
    "Chrome/142.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
)


class PortalError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message: str, code: str = ""):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code


@dataclass
class ServerInfo:
    portal_url: str
    engine: str = ""
    api_version: str = ""
    pub_key: str = ""
    title: str = ""
    client_user_hint: str = ""
    client_password_hint: str = ""
    auth_server: str = ""
    client_save_pass: bool = False
    need_auth: bool = True


@dataclass
class DeviceInfo:
    device_id: str
    registered: bool = False
    check_result: str = ""
    ip: str = ""
    mac: str = ""
    ascid: str = ""
    dev_name: str = ""
    os_name: str = ""


@dataclass
class LoginResult:
    success: bool
    message: str
    code: str = ""
    token: str = ""
    user_name: str = ""
    needs_two_factor: bool = False


def _truthy(value: Any) -> bool:
    return value is True or value == 1 or str(value).lower() in ("1", "true", "yes")


class PortalClient:
    def __init__(self, config: AppConfig):
        self.config = config.clone()
        self.base_url = normalize_base_url(config.portal_url)
        self.api_version = (config.api_version or "6039.3746").strip()
        self.ascid = (config.ascid or "").strip()
        self.session = requests.Session()
        self.session.trust_env = False
        self.session.proxies = {}
        self.session.headers.update(
            {
                "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
                "Accept": "application/json, text/plain, */*",
                "Accept-Language": "zh-CN,zh;q=0.9",
                "X-Requested-With": "XMLHttpRequest",
            }
        )
        self._server: Optional[ServerInfo] = None
        self._server_at = 0.0
        self._device: Optional[DeviceInfo] = None
        self._device_at = 0.0

    def close(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.session.close()
        except Exception:
            pass

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ 门户信息
    def get_server_info(self, force: bool = False) -> ServerInfo:
        if not force and self._server is not None and time.time() - self._server_at < 300:
            return self._server
        info = self._fetch_server_info()
        self._server = info
        self._server_at = time.time()
        return info

    def _fetch_server_info(self) -> ServerInfo:
        query = self._query()
        root = self._get_json("server/info", query)
        code = int(root.get("errcode") or 0)

        if code == 21101015 and self._refresh_api_version():
            root = self._get_json("server/info", self._query())
            code = int(root.get("errcode") or 0)

        if code != 0:
            raise PortalError(friendly_message(code, str(root.get("errmsg") or "")), str(code))

        data = root.get("data") or {}
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise PortalError("认证服务器返回的数据不完整。", "NODATA")

        admin = data.get("ADMINISTRATORINFO") or {}
        client_auth = data.get("ClientAuth") or {}
        user = data.get("User") or {}
        client_check = data.get("CLIENTCHECK") or {}

        info = ServerInfo(
            portal_url=self.base_url,
            engine=str(data.get("Engine") or ""),
            api_version=self.api_version,
            pub_key=str(data.get("pubKey") or ""),
            title=str(admin.get("sTitle") or admin.get("indextitle") or ""),
            client_user_hint=str(client_auth.get("ClientUser") or ""),
            client_password_hint=str(client_auth.get("ClientPassword") or ""),
            auth_server=str(user.get("AuthServer") or ""),
            client_save_pass=_truthy(client_check.get("ClientSavePass")),
            need_auth=_truthy(client_check.get("IsAuth")),
        )
        return info

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ 设备信息
    def get_device_info(self, force: bool = False) -> DeviceInfo:
        if not force and self._device is not None and time.time() - self._device_at < 300:
            return self._device
        info = self._fetch_device_info()
        self._device = info
        self._device_at = time.time()
        return info

    def _fetch_device_info(self) -> DeviceInfo:
        body: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
            ("gettype", "ipgetmac"),
            ("deviceid", ""),
            ("license", ""),
            ("UrlAswid", ""),
            ("BrowserFingerprint", ""),
            ("forbid", ""),
            ("basIP", ""),
            ("firstUrl", ""),
            ("Mac", ""),
            ("is_guest", "0"),
            ("is_mobile", "0"),
            ("os_platform", "Windows 10"),
            ("browser", "Chrome/142.0.0.0"),
            ("UrlAscid", self.ascid),
            ("wlanusermac", ""),
            ("doorFrom", ""),
            ("doorIP", ""),
            ("doorMAC", ""),
        ]
        query = f"?local_lguage_set=zh&cache={now_ms()}"
        root = self._post_json("device/infoprocess", query, body)
        code = int(root.get("errcode") or 0)
        if code != 0:
            raise PortalError(friendly_message(code, str(root.get("errmsg") or "")), str(code))

        data = root.get("data") or {}
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise PortalError("认证服务器未返回设备信息。", "NODEVICE")
        device_id = str(data.get("DeviceID") or "")
        if not device_id:
            raise PortalError("认证服务器返回的设备标识为空，请稍后重试。", "NODEVICE")

        return DeviceInfo(
            device_id=device_id,
            registered=_truthy(data.get("Registered")),
            check_result=str(data.get("CheckResult") or ""),
            ip=str(data.get("IP") or ""),
            mac=str(data.get("Mac") or ""),
            ascid=str(data.get("AscID") or ""),
            dev_name=str(data.get("DevName") or ""),
            os_name=str(data.get("OSName") or ""),
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ 登录
    def login(self, username: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
        try:
            return self._login(username, password, allow_version_retry=True)
        except PortalError as exc:
            LOGGER.warning("登录失败: %s (%s)", exc, exc.code)
            return LoginResult(False, str(exc), exc.code)
        except requests.RequestException as exc:
            LOGGER.warning("登录网络异常: %s", exc)
            return LoginResult(False, f"无法连接认证服务器：{exc}", "NETWORK")
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            LOGGER.exception("登录异常")
            return LoginResult(False, f"登录异常：{exc}", "EXCEPTION")

    def _login(self, username: str, password: str, allow_version_retry: bool) -> LoginResult:
        server = self.get_server_info()
        if not server.pub_key:
            raise PortalError("认证服务器未返回加密公钥，请检查认证地址。", "NOPUBKEY")
        device = self.get_device_info()
        if not device.device_id:
            raise PortalError("未能获取本机设备标识，请确认已连接校园网。", "NODEVICE")

        encrypted = rsa_encrypt(password, server.pub_key)
        user_name64 = base64.b64encode((username or "").encode("utf-8")).decode("ascii")

        body: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
            ("user_name", user_name64),
            ("deviceid", device.device_id),
            ("idp", ""),
            ("tokenId", ""),
            ("remoteIp", ""),
            ("password", encrypted),
            ("hintOver", "0"),
            ("autoAuth", "0"),
            ("verify_code", ""),
            ("type", "User"),
        ]
        query = f"?local_lguage_set=zh&cache={now_ms()}"
        root = self._post_json("auth/index", query, body)
        code = int(root.get("errcode") or 0)

        if code == 0:
            data = root.get("data") or {}
            if isinstance(data, dict) and _truthy(data.get("FactorAuth")):
                return LoginResult(
                    False,
                    "该账号启用了二次验证，请打开认证网页完成短信/二次验证。",
                    "FactorAuth",
                    needs_two_factor=True,
                )
            return LoginResult(
                True,
                "登录成功",
                "",
                str(data.get("Token") or "") if isinstance(data, dict) else "",
                str(data.get("UserName") or "") if isinstance(data, dict) else "",
            )

        if code == 21101015 and allow_version_retry and self._refresh_api_version():
            return self._login(username, password, allow_version_retry=False)

        return LoginResult(False, friendly_message(code, str(root.get("errmsg") or "")), str(code))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ HTTP
    def _query(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"?basIP=&ascid={self.ascid}"
            f"&firsturl=&version={self.api_version}"
            f"&agentPromotion=&local_lguage_set=zh&cache={now_ms()}"
        )

    def _headers(self, referer: bool = True) -> dict[str, str]:
        headers = {
            "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
            "Accept": "application/json, text/plain, */*",
            "Accept-Language": "zh-CN,zh;q=0.9",
            "X-Requested-With": "XMLHttpRequest",
        }
        if referer:
            headers["Referer"] = self.base_url + UI_PATH
        return headers

    def _get_json(self, api_path: str, query: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        path_query = API_ROOT + api_path + query
        headers = self._headers()
        headers["Session-Num"] = session_num(path_query, None)
        response = self.session.get(
            self.base_url + path_query,
            headers=headers,
            timeout=(5, 15),
            allow_redirects=False,
        )
        return self._parse_response(response)

    def _post_json(
        self,
        api_path: str,
        query: str,
        body: Iterable[tuple[str, str]],
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        body_list = list(body)
        path_query = API_ROOT + api_path + query
        headers = self._headers()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8"
        headers["Session-Num"] = session_num(path_query, body_list)
        encoded = urlencode(body_list, doseq=False)
        response = self.session.post(
            self.base_url + path_query,
            data=encoded.encode("utf-8"),
            headers=headers,
            timeout=(5, 15),
            allow_redirects=False,
        )
        return self._parse_response(response)

    def _parse_response(self, response: requests.Response) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if 300 <= response.status_code < 400:
            location = response.headers.get("Location", "")
            raise PortalError(f"认证服务器发生重定向：{location}", "REDIRECT")
        text = response.content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        if not text.strip():
            raise PortalError(f"认证服务器返回空响应（HTTP {response.status_code}）。", "EMPTY")
        try:
            root = json.loads(text)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            LOGGER.warning("认证服务器返回非 JSON 内容: %s", text[:200])
            raise PortalError(f"认证服务器返回格式异常：{exc}", "BADJSON") from exc
        if not isinstance(root, dict):
            raise PortalError("认证服务器返回格式异常。", "BADJSON")
        return root

    def _refresh_api_version(self) -> bool:
        try:
            response = self.session.get(
                self.base_url + "/access/ui/js/index.js",
                timeout=(5, 25),
                allow_redirects=False,
            )
            text = response.content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            match = re.search(
                r"""getGlobalServerDispose[\s\S]{0,1200}?version\s*=\s*"([0-9]{3,5}\.[0-9]{3,5})"""",
                text,
            )
            if not match:
                match = re.search(r"""version\s*=\s*"([0-9]{3,5}\.[0-9]{3,5})"""", text)
            if match:
                version = match.group(1)
                if version != self.api_version:
                    LOGGER.info("检测到门户版本更新: %s -> %s", self.api_version, version)
                    self.api_version = version
                    self._server = None
                    return True
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            LOGGER.warning("自动获取门户版本失败: %s", exc)
        return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 工具函数
def session_num(path_query: str, body: Optional[Iterable[tuple[str, str]]]) -> str:
    raw = path_query
    if body:
        for key, value in body:
            raw += f"&{key}={value}"
    sanitized = re.sub(r"""[^0-9a-zA-Z=&()/._?'"<>]""", "", raw)
    return hashlib.md5(sanitized.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def friendly_message(code: int, server_message: str = "") -> str:
    if code == 21100006:
        return "认证请求被拒绝（门户地址或版本不匹配，请检查认证地址）。"
    if code == 21101015:
        return "认证门户版本已更新，请稍后重试。"
    if code == 21134001:
        return "手机号不存在或尚未开通 I教育平台认证。"
    if code == 21134002:
        return "密码错误，请重新输入。"
    if code in (21133003, 21133015, 21133017):
        return "密码已过期，请先在认证网页修改密码。"
    if code == 21120030:
        return "需要在认证网页完成设备或账号确认。"
    return server_message or f"登录失败（错误码 {code}）。"


def _read_element(data: bytes, position: int) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    if position < 0 or position + 2 > len(data):
        raise PortalError("公钥数据不完整。", "BADKEY")
    tag = data[position]
    position += 1
    first = data[position]
    position += 1
    if first & 0x80:
        count = first & 0x7F
        if count <= 0 or count > 4 or position + count > len(data):
            raise PortalError("公钥长度字段异常。", "BADKEY")
        length = int.from_bytes(data[position : position + count], "big")
        position += count
    else:
        length = first
    if length < 0 or position + length > len(data):
        raise PortalError("公钥内容越界。", "BADKEY")
    return tag, position, length, position + length


def parse_public_key(pem: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    if not pem or "PUBLIC KEY" not in pem:
        raise PortalError("认证服务器公钥格式异常。", "BADKEY")
    pkcs1 = "RSA PUBLIC KEY" in pem
    base64_text = re.sub(r"-----[^-]+-----", "", pem)
    base64_text = re.sub(r"\s+", "", base64_text)
    try:
        der = base64.b64decode(base64_text, validate=True)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        raise PortalError("认证服务器公钥不是有效的 Base64。", "BADKEY") from exc

    _tag, outer_start, _outer_len, _outer_next = _read_element(der, 0)
    if pkcs1:
        _tag, mod_start, mod_len, mod_next = _read_element(der, outer_start)
        _tag, exp_start, exp_len, _ = _read_element(der, mod_next)
    else:
        _tag, _alg_start, _alg_len, alg_next = _read_element(der, outer_start)
        _tag, bit_start, _bit_len, _ = _read_element(der, alg_next)
        key_pos = bit_start + 1
        _tag, seq_start, _seq_len, _ = _read_element(der, key_pos)
        _tag, mod_start, mod_len, mod_next = _read_element(der, seq_start)
        _tag, exp_start, exp_len, _ = _read_element(der, mod_next)

    modulus = int.from_bytes(der[mod_start : mod_start + mod_len], "big")
    exponent = int.from_bytes(der[exp_start : exp_start + exp_len], "big")
    if modulus.bit_length() < 512 or exponent <= 1:
        raise PortalError("认证服务器公钥长度异常。", "BADKEY")
    return modulus, exponent


def rsa_encrypt(plain_text: str, pem: str) -> str:
    """RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 加密，与浏览器端 CryptoJS/JSEncrypt 的结果兼容。"""
    if not plain_text:
        raise PortalError("密码不能为空。", "PASSWORD")
    modulus, exponent = parse_public_key(pem)
    message = plain_text.encode("utf-8")
    key_size = (modulus.bit_length() + 7) // 8
    padding_length = key_size - len(message) - 3
    if padding_length < 8:
        raise PortalError("密码过长，无法使用门户公钥加密。", "PASSWORDTOOLONG")

    padding = bytearray()
    while len(padding) < padding_length:
        chunk = secrets.token_bytes(padding_length - len(padding))
        padding.extend(b for b in chunk if b != 0)
    encoded = b"\x00\x02" + bytes(padding[:padding_length]) + b"\x00" + message
    cipher = pow(int.from_bytes(encoded, "big"), exponent, modulus)
    return base64.b64encode(cipher.to_bytes(key_size, "big")).decode("ascii")","file_path":"C:\Users\HiteVision\Documents\deepseek-harness\default-workspace\campus-net-login-py\portal.py"}
